meta.title: Suno Style field: how to specify sound and vocals
meta.note: Style box = genre, mood, instruments, vocal identity, arrangement arc. Lyrics box = words plus [Verse]/[Chorus] tags and per-section singer labels. Vocal phrases are steering cues, not hard locks.

unspecified.use_when: Let Suno pick a singer from genre bias. Pop often leans female; rock/hip-hop often lean male.
style_examples: indie pop, warm, clear lead vocal, jangly guitar, punchy drums, polished mix, sparse verse, wide chorus
lo-fi hip hop, late night, lead vocal, dusty drums, warm bass, vinyl texture, short intro, fade out
notes: Genre will often decide the voice.
Do not write male or female anywhere if you want it open.

style_examples: pop rock, anthemic, male lead vocal, electric guitar, live drums, warm bass, sparse verse, wide chorus, hard stop
R&B ballad, intimate, smooth male vocal, Rhodes, brushed drums, restrained verse, layered final chorus
notes: Repeat male in Style and as a Lyrics anchor for fewer mid-song gender swaps.
Add register (baritone / tenor) if the genre keeps flipping the voice.

style_examples: synth pop, bright, breathy female vocal, analog synths, tight drums, short intro, wide chorus, fade out
cinematic ballad, emotional, powerful female vocal, piano, strings, intimate verse, final lift
notes: Repeat female in Style and as a Lyrics anchor.
Pop defaults female often; still specify if you need it stable.

duet.use_when: Two distinct singers. Must say duet and name both voices.
style_phrases: one male vocalist and one female vocalist
style_modifiers: female-led chorus with male lower harmony
gritty male rapper and powerhouse female vocalist
interaction_phrases: never both at once until the chorus
style_examples: pop ballad, male and female duet, alternating verses, harmonized chorus, piano, soft drums, gradual build, final lift
country duet, one male vocalist and one female vocalist, call and response verses, blended chorus, acoustic guitar, pedal steel, restrained verse, wide chorus
R&B duet, male and female vocals, verses sung separately, chorus together, Rhodes, tight groove, intimate, layered chorus
notes: Put the word duet in Style. 'male and female vocals' alone is weaker.
Name roles once in Style, then the same names in Lyrics tags.
Say how they interact: alternate / call-and-response / harmony together.
Unspecified duet often collapses into one blended voice.

choir.use_when: Group or choral vocals: gospel choir, a cappella, gang vocals, chants.
style_examples: modern dynamic gospel, majestic, gospel choir, massive choir harmony, cinematic strings, gradual build, final lift
raw root gospel, a cappella vocals, call and response, handclaps, foot stomps, unpolished
notes: Name the choir type (gospel, Gregorian, gang) for a steadier result.
Combine with a lead vocal phrase when a soloist should sit on top of the choir.

terms.definition: A breathy, soft, airy high voice — the common, relaxed 'fake voice'.
A resonant, focused high register felt around the crown/forehead, clearer and more core than falsetto.
The full, chest-resonant natural voice used in normal speech and powerful singing.
A smooth blend of chest and head/falsetto voice that keeps power and core tone through the high range.
A relaxed-throat, creaky, rattling low-register vibration effect.
Deliberately sliding pitch up or down into or out of a note rather than landing on it straight.
Singing purposely flat or sharp of true pitch for character.
Approaching a note from slightly below its true pitch and sliding up into it.
Fast melodic embellishments (fake/riffing) that break a line into many quick moving notes.
A fast, regular up-and-down pitch wobble on sustained notes.
Pushing chest voice powerfully into the high range instead of switching to falsetto.
A raspy, rumbling growl/snarl texture, common in rock and jazz.
A whisper-like vocal with a lot of breath mixed into the tone.
Rapidly flipping between chest voice and falsetto, sometimes used as a pop accent.
